answer: Convex influence weighting makes splitting one track record across clones a losing trade. A seat's vote and reward share equal its reputation squared, where reputation is the count of passed answers signed by that one key, at most one per epoch, and no cipher or relabelling can move it to another key. An operator with 20 passes holds weight 400 as one seat; spread over 10 clones of 2 passes each, the farm totals just 40, a canyon of lost influence. Every fake must grow its own plume of graded work from zero, so each extra identity only dilutes the attacker further.
